applicant_utility.summary: This is a full-tuition-for-four-years award attached to UIC admission, not a separate competition: submit the undergraduate application and admitted international students are considered automatically, with the offer letter arriving inside the admission packet. The waived amount equals the International Students Track tuition of 8,202,000 KRW per semester (2026), so you still need funds for miscellaneous fees (about 56,000-61,000 KRW per semester), housing, food and personal costs. The one continuing condition is your semester GPA - the scholarship is re-checked each semester and lapses in the following semester if you fall below the required level.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-Korean high-school graduates (with non-Korean parents) seeking an English-medium liberal-arts and STEM bachelor's in Seoul who can keep a strong GPA and can fund living costs on top of tuition.
application_readiness_checklist: Start apostille or Korean consulate authentication of transcripts and graduation certificates months ahead - hard copies must physically arrive at the UIC Office by the deadline, not just be posted
From the 2027 intake, line up English proof early: a recognized test report, a diploma from an English-official-language country, or a school Medium of Instruction certificate
Prepare the Letter of Consent & Verification plus passport copies for you and both parents
Budget the KRW 150,000 (USD 150) application fee - UIC offers no fee waiver
Diarise the online interview window (11-12 December 2026 for the Spring 2027 round) and keep the phone reachable for verification calls
common_rejection_risks: Documents arriving after the physical submission deadline - UIC states the deadline will not be extended under any circumstances and failure to submit any required document disqualifies
Any Korean dual citizenship in the family (student or parent), which removes International Students Track eligibility entirely
GED, home-schooled or cyber-schooled certificates, which UIC does not treat as a high school diploma
Failing to maintain the required GPA after admission, which costs the scholarship in the following semester
Un-notarized kinship or parent-relationship documents, especially for applicants with Chinese nationality
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Miscellaneous fees of 56,000 KRW per semester (61,000 KRW in the first semester), plus housing, food, transport, insurance and personal expenses in Seoul - the award waives tuition only.
document_audit: All documents must be in English or accompanied by a notarized English translation

Transcripts and graduation certificates need Apostille (Hague Convention countries) or Korean consulate authentication; documents from Chinese high schools need a CSHI report or the specified certificate set
Standardized scores (Duolingo, IELTS, TOEFL, SAT, AP) reported directly to Yonsei must also be flagged to uicadm@yonsei.ac.kr with your English name and test date, and a hard copy posted
alerts: The 2nd Round (Fall 2027 entry) date is only 'March, 2027 (TBD)' - check UIC announcements rather than assuming last year's calendar
Spring-entry students receive visa, tuition and enrolment emails in late December; fall-entry in late June
The scholarship is conditional on GPA every single semester, not just at entry
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Online application (UIC site or Common App) plus physical delivery of the full document pack to the UIC Office, then an online interview; the scholarship decision rides on the admission decision with no extra form.

applicant_utility.summary: This is an automatic per-semester top-up, not something you apply for: enrol full-time on the international track in regular semesters and the Graduate School pays KRW 2,000,000 per semester for a master's, KRW 3,000,000 for a PhD and KRW 2,000,000 for the integrated programme, over 4 semesters (6 for the integrated track). It stacks nothing with a full Graduate School tuition scholarship - if you hold one, you are excluded - so the Companion Scholarship is most valuable to students paying tuition who need a stipend on top. Medicine, Dentistry, Nursing, contract-based programmes and Mirae Campus students are excluded, so check your college before counting on it.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Full-time international-track master's, PhD and integrated students at Yonsei's Seoul campus who do not hold a full tuition scholarship and are outside the excluded medical and contract programmes.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are enrolled through the international student admission track, not another category
Verify your college is not Medicine, Dentistry or Nursing and your programme is not contract-based
Keep enrolment in regular semesters (avoid leave of absence, which breaks the regular-semester basis of the award)
Budget the stipend as per-semester income across the standard 4-semester (6-semester integrated) support period
common_rejection_risks: Holding a full Graduate School tuition scholarship, which excludes you from this award
Enrolment at Mirae Campus or in a contract-based programme
Non-regular-semester status (for example extended or non-standard registration)
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The award is a fixed per-semester scholarship amount; tuition (unless separately waived), housing, insurance and all other living costs sit outside it.
document_audit: No documents are submitted for this award - but your international-track admission paperwork is what proves eligibility, so keep it accessible
alerts: The award stops at 4 regular semesters for master's and PhD students (6 for integrated) - plan funding for the remainder of your programme
Taking a leave of absence or moving to a non-regular semester status interrupts eligibility
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Nothing to submit: the Graduate School assesses enrolled international-track students against the published table each regular semester.
